title: Applied Materials opens a $5 billion center to help build the next generation of AI chips
source_used: CTech (page text read from the article data in the HTML); date and partner quote checked on Evertiq
key_facts: Applied Materials opened its EPIC Center (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) in Sunnyvale, California; the company's press release is dated 12 Oct 2026 (Evertiq).
Founding partners: TSMC, Intel, Samsung Electronics, Micron Technology and SK hynix.
Innovation partners include Broadcom, Advantest, SCREEN, Kioxia and Besi; university researchers come from Stanford, UC Berkeley, UCLA, Arizona State University and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.
The aim is to develop materials, equipment and production processes in parallel rather than one after another.
The facility spans about 600,000 square feet with nearly four acres of cleanroom; construction took more than six million labor hours.
Capital spending is expected to scale to about USD 5 billion over time as customer projects start; it is not money already spent.
Shorter learning cycles and faster move to high-volume production are objectives, not results demonstrated publicly.
quote_evidence: Those benefits remain objectives of the project, rather than results that have yet been demonstrated publicly.
The company expects capital spending to scale over time to approximately $5 billion as customer projects commence, rather than treating the entire sum as money already spent.
The founding partners include TSMC, Intel, Samsung Electronics, Micron Technology and SK hynix, companies that compete across parts of the semiconductor market.
why_it_matters_hint: Rival chipmakers are sharing one development site to bring new AI chip manufacturing methods to market sooner.
notes: CTech page text sits in the page data, not in visible paragraphs; read from there. Earlier partner announcements for this centre were in our 1 Oct (Kioxia) and 7 Oct (Intel) editions. Doubt: Financial-News.co.uk notes the 5 billion figure is a ceiling and the 2023 plan was up to 4 billion; not used in the entry.
